BC_description: The partial application feature of async.applyEach has been removed. Previously, calling async.applyEach(fns) returned a function that accepted arguments for later partial application, such as runFns(arg1, arg2, cb). Now, async.applyEach only supports an immediate callback or awaiting its result; you can no longer use applyEach to build a partially-applied function that waits for arguments. Code patterns relying on partial application via applyEach will break and must be refactored to provide all arguments directly to the original functions, or by using a wrapper function if needed.
